Point P is at the endpoint of the lower-left bottom side, and line segment PQ slants from P upward to the right to point Q on the right vertical side. X, Q, Y are marked on the right vertical side, where Y is 1 unit above the bottom side, X is 2 units above the bottom side, and Q is between X and Y. The region below line segment PQ is composed of one unit square on the right side and a triangle with base 5. Reasoning: The area of the whole octagon is 10, and PQ bisects the area, so the area below PQ is 5. Let the height of Q from the bottom side be h. The area below PQ equals the area 1 of the right unit square plus the area of the triangle; the base of this triangle is 5 and the height is h, so the area is (1/2)·5h. Therefore 1 + (1/2)·5h = 5. From the image, read that \(P\) is on the lower-left baseline, \(Q\) lies on the vertical segment \(XY\), with \(Y\) one unit above the bottom and \(X\) two units above the bottom. The region below \(PQ\) consists of the rightmost unit square plus a triangle whose horizontal base from \(P\) to the vertical through \(Q\) has length \(5\). Then \(1+\frac12\cdot 5h=5\), giving \(h=\frac85\). Since \(Y\) is at height \(1\) and \(X\) is at height \(2\), \(QY=h-1=\frac35\) and \(XQ=2-h=\frac25\), so \(XQ/QY=\frac23\).
